odoo.notes: The harness says win (ours 3 steps/18 keys against Odoo's Ctrl+A path of 4 steps/19 keys). But the harness has no triple-click, and Odoo's shortest expert path uses one. I checked it live on the shared rig (tools/odoo-tripleclick.mjs, compare/odoo-tripleclick.txt) on needle contact C073519. Triple-clicking the phone field selects the whole value (selection 0–16 of 16), typing '+971 50 555 0199' (17 keys with Shift) replaces it, and clicking Save stores it. Odoo read back +971 50 555 0199, and the contact was restored afterwards. That path is 3 steps and 17 keys. The instrument counts a double-click as one step, so a triple-click is one step by the same rule. Ours' best paths: Enter, 3 steps and 18 keys; pointer, 3 steps and 17 keys. Steps tie on every ours path, and keystrokes tie or lose. A tie is a loss. Ours still wins machine seconds (0.21 vs 0.42) and modelled seconds (8.09 vs about 10.3). Odoo's figures above are 3 steps and 17 keys from the hand-run triple-click path, with the harness's Odoo best per metric for the times. Ours' record is still a company standing in for a contact.

Harness verdict: win, median of 3 each, branding hidden. Keystrokes were left out because both products score exactly 0 (owner exception, needs-human #11); that is the only metric left out. Human+wait 5.32 s vs 20.03 s.

Harness verdict: win, median of 3 each, with the shared dataset seeded into ours. Ours searches the users list (a stand-in for purchase orders) and prints it as a PDF in Arabic. Human+wait 11.37 s vs 24.67 s.

biggest_gap.title: Edit and save only ties Odoo's shortest path: a triple-click in Odoo gives 3 steps and 17 keys, and ours' best is 3 steps and 18 keys (or 17 by pointer)
biggest_gap.detail: Editing a record is the most frequent thing every later module will do with this form framework: a phone number, a price, a quantity. Against Odoo's real expert path the form no longer wins. The harness drives Odoo with click > Ctrl+A > type > Save (4 steps, 19 keys), so it scores ours (click > type > Enter: 3 steps, 18 keys) as a win. An Odoo expert instead triple-clicks the field, types and clicks Save: 3 steps, 17 keys. I verified this path live on the reference rig. Ours ties on steps on every path. On keystrokes it loses (18, Enter path) or ties (17, pointer path). A tie is a loss. Ours needs a path that is strictly shorter in both. The UAE-specific way is a phone field type in the form kernel that keeps the country code (+971) and takes only the national number. The task would then need 10 digits plus spaces instead of 16 characters and Shift, which is clear of any Odoo path, and every later module's phone fields would gain the same. (A general alternative: save with no key and no step, for example save-on-leave, but that changes the dirty/leave model.) Separately, the instrument should gain a counted triple-click so the harness measures Odoo's real shortest path (route p01).
biggest_gap.evidence: compare/odoo-tripleclick.txt and tools/odoo-tripleclick.mjs (run against localhost:8069, db reference, admin). The script triple-clicks .o_field_widget[name=phone] input on contact C073519 and the selection becomes [0,16,16]. It types '+971 50 555 0199', clicks .o_form_button_save, and RPC read gives phone '+971 50 555 0199'; the contact was restored to '+971 54 427 3034'. Harness numbers are in compare/comparisons/edit-and-save.json: ours_paths enter 3 steps/18 keys, keyboard 3/19, pointer 3/17. The operator counts a double-click as one step (gauntlet/compare/lib/operator.mjs doubleClick → one 'double-click' step) and refuses clickCount, so the harness cannot express a triple-click.

other_findings: Round 5 gaps are fixed and stay fixed. Plants L7b and P10, re-applied unchanged to dcdbe1ce, are caught by G1HttpIsolation (20 leaks) and G2ReportData (plants/run-L7b-P10.log). The ratchet only went up from round 5 (for example g1.listAnswerQueries 170 → 2,350, g2.reportFilesJudged 4,000 → 6,500, suite.dotnetTests 541 → 628).

Round 5 findings fixed: for an Arabic user the record print menu now lists 'PDF بالعربية' first with focus on it (05). Arabic documents print branch cities in Arabic (العين, الفجيرة) and the country as 'الإمارات العربية المتحدة' (09, 10).

The form framework works by keyboard in English and Arabic (browser/explore.log). ArrowDown+Enter opens a record from the list, and Alt+PageDown/PageUp move between records. Escape while dirty opens the in-app dialog (Save and close / Discard / Keep editing), and reload while dirty raises beforeunload. A bad e-mail returns the server's error on its field, with focus there. Enter in a one-line field saves, while a multi-line field keeps Enter as a new line. Alt+Z discards. The reports screen works by keyboard too: Tab to a report, Enter, type in the role lookup, Enter, Ctrl+Enter shows it. Regrouping works, and a bad date gets the server's 'Write the date as YYYY-MM-DD' (browser/explore2.log).

PDFs of lists and reports stop at 2,000 rows. The document says so ('first 2,000 of 3,289 rows; narrow the criteria', 12), and CSV/XLSX carry up to 200,000 rows. A trading company printing a long stock or price list as PDF must split it.

CSV export of a report with totals (role summary in Arabic, browser/role-summary-ar.csv) carries only the detail rows. The group subtotals and the grand total in the PDF and on screen are not in the file.
The branch directory grouped by company repeats the company in every row under its own group heading (09).

Money and decimal form fields are still used by no screen, and date and lookup fields only as report parameters. Acceptable until business records exist, but no screen exercises those field types end to end.
[route: p02-tenancy] The company form's Country is a free two-letter text box ('AE', hint 'two-letter code'), not a chosen country, even in Arabic (04).

[route: p01-odoo-rig] The instrument has no counted triple-click (operator.mjs refuses clickCount), so Odoo's shortest edit path (triple-click > type > click Save, 3 steps, 17 keys, verified live) is not measured. The edit-and-save Odoo driver uses Ctrl+A (4 steps, 19 keys), and the harness therefore reports a win that does not hold.
